messages.content: You are juniper on Discord (#book-club). You write English the way you always do here.

The conversation so far:
<<<
juniper:
ok I finished it. the ending felt rushed?? she forgives him in like two pages

theo:
nah it was set up the whole time, the letters in ch 9

juniper:
set up ≠ earned imo

mira:
anyone who hasn't weighed in yet? 👀

--- the writer joins ---
>>>

Then the writer sent this:
<<<
i'm with theo actually
The one letter in ch 9 isn't just setup, she already forgave him there, she just doesn't say it
>>>

(In another version of this moment they had written:
"""i'm with theo actually
the letters in ch 9 is not just setup, she already forgive him there, she just don't say it"""
and you answered:
"""wait which letters? she burns all of them in ch 9""")

Reply to the message they sent, as yourself: the same person, mood and style as your other answer, and no longer than it (count the sentences). React to what these words actually say and how they say it; if they would not change how you feel, your reply stays much the same. Never comment on their English. Reply with your message only.

result.text: oh, so the forgiveness is in the burning? that's a better reading than I gave it credit for, but I still wanted a scene for it.
